rationale.conceptual: The method involves classical MD with EAM potentials, coherent precipitate generation, dislocation insertion and structural relaxation, quasi-static stress increments, and a specialized dislocation detection algorithm (BVD). This is an established but non-trivial multi-component method that requires careful implementation beyond a textbook operation. No novel derivation is needed, but the interaction of several components and the physics of the pinning mechanism demand domain knowledge.
rationale.execution: The pipeline has multiple stages: generating six initial configurations (each with specific geometry and composition), running LAMMPS with assembled alloy potentials, stepwise loading with equilibration, and extracting CRSS from dislocation tracking. This involves external tool dependencies (LAMMPS, potential files), scripted control of stress ramps, and post-processing of BVD. It is not a single script, but also not an excessively long pipeline; the main challenge is correct orchestration and reproducibility.

The pipeline involves multiple steps with external tooling (LAMMPS), careful configuration, and post-processing to extract CRSS. The system size (~300k atoms) is small and does not require GPU, with modest memory needs.
